body:
Independent fresh-context review of the exact head `38c90ea258bea7a22412490eb9fc8995f6638434`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Both verdicts: APPROVE — no P0 findings, no P1 findings, no P2 findings.**

What the reviews verified:

- The streamed text reaches the client byte for byte. A differential fuzz over 24000 randomised trials and a separate 1000-case seeded chunk-boundary sweep, both against independently written models of the documented rule, found no mismatch.
- A crawl-status line is dropped whole, including one split across deltas, one that follows a long run of spaces, and one that ends the answer without a newline; a crawl marker in the middle of a line is ordinary text and the line is no longer cut off.
- A tool call that shares a line with a crawl-status line is delivered exactly once at every chunk boundary, and the crawl text never reaches the client.
- The upstream response is closed on every exit path: normal completion, the tool-call short-circuit, a client disconnect, an exception inside the generator, and a stream closed before the first chunk is read.
- The non-streaming path is unchanged.

The reviews drove three rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code: a line whose middle held the crawl marker was truncated and the rest of it dropped; a tool call on a line that was dropped was lost with it; and a crawl-status line at the end of an answer without a newline reached the client.

Two bounds are stated in the changelog rather than hidden: a line in a stream ends only at a newline, and a crawl-status line is dropped whole while it is still undecided and fits in the holdback of 8192 characters.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
